When Aerdy became an empire, its leaders set out to crush the troublesome barbarians pushing down from the Thillonrian Peninsula and settling the strip of land between the Rakers and Grendep Bay. Being poor sailors, the Aerdians attacked overland, sending strong parties north to drive the northerners home. After many sharp skirmishes a large imperial force was routed, and open war began.

The Fruztii tribes had fallen back before the Aerdians, but they called on their kin, and those hardy fighters poured south by land and sea, eager for battle and loot. More than 10,000 gathered and attacked the works being built at Spinecastle. A relief army met them in a pitched battle; most of the barbarians died, along with several thousand imperial soldiers. The new fief took its name from what that fight left behind: the Battle of the Shamblefield, or Caldni Vir's Charge.

In 560 CY humanoid hordes (Euroz, Kell, Eiger and others) began raiding the Bone March, and the next year the raids became a full invasion. In 563 the land fell. Its lord was killed and its army killed or enslaved, and the human inhabitants were enslaved or slain too. One or more humanoid chiefs now rule the whole territory; exact details are unknown. The humanoids came in through the mountains and now use those trails to raid the Pale, Ratik and even Nyrond, though crossing the Flinty Hills is very dangerous because gnomes still hold out there. Border fighting goes on without end along the Teesar Torrent and in the Blemu Hills of Aerdy's North Province, though some say the Overking would happily make peace with the humanoids to his north and recruit them into his armies.

Source: Guide p.20. Rewritten in plain words.

RulerHer Fey Majesty, Yolande, Queen of Celene, Lady Rhalta of All Elvenkind
CapitalEnstad (pop. 6,950)
Population20,000
Demi-humansGray Elves (9,500), Sylvan Elves (8,000), Gnomes (13,500), Halflings
HumanoidsNone
Resourcesfoodstuffs, cloth, silver
Ruler's class and levelYolande, F 7/MU 11 (Glossography p.17)

This small land west of the Wild Coast, beyond the Welkwood, has long been ruled by elves. They are good folk, but they do not welcome strangers, with reason, so little is known for certain about Celene or its court. The realm is friendly with the Ulek states. An alliance of Celene and the Uleks waged the campaigns that drove every humanoid out of the Lortmil Mountains, although the beaten humanoids then invaded and took over the Pomarj. A small number of humans and half-elves live in Celene, many of them serving in its army, for there is constant war with the humanoid tribes of the Pomarj in the Suss Forest and beyond the Jewel River.

pages.name: Dyvers, Free and Independent City of

text.content:
Source: Guide p.20. Rewritten in plain words.

RulerHis Excellency Margus, the Magister of Dyvers
Population42,000+ (city) 53,000 (total, including surrounding area)
Demi-humansSome
HumanoidsFew
Resourcesshipbuilding supplies
Ruler's class and levelMargus, T 17 (Glossography p.17)

Dyvers sits where the Velverdyva River meets the Nyr Dyv, the Lake of Unknown Depths. That makes it a key trading center and a busy port, with lake and river traffic from as far off as Perrenland, Bissel, Nyrond, Urnst, the Pale and Tenh, and now and then even envoys from Iuz.

The city was once part of the Viceroyalty of Ferrond and gave heavily in money, goods and men to the war that founded the Kingdom of Furyondy. The Gentry of Dyvers saw Furyondy's alliance and close ties with Veluna as confining, so the city declared independence in 526 CY, and King Thrommel II let it go unchallenged. Dyvers claims about 2,000 square miles as its own, including the islands at the river mouth, though its Magisters have taken care to claim nothing on the north bank of the river. The city has 1,000 marines and an army twice that size, all very well armed and equipped.

Source: Guide p.20. Rewritten in plain words.

RulerHis Sublime Magnificence, the Caliph of Ekbir, Xargun
CapitalEkbir (pop. 29,400)
Population250,000
Demi-humansDoubtful
HumanoidsFew
Resourcesfoodstuffs, cloth
Ruler's class and levelXargun, C 16 (Glossography p.17)

Ekbir is the strongest Baklunish city in the Flanaess. Survivors of the Invoked Devastation founded it as a small port, and it soon became a market for the nomads' goods too. The village became a walled town and the town a thriving city. Ekbir rules a sizable territory and has a large war fleet. Its army is mostly light and medium cavalry; its standing force is said to be about 5,000 soldiers, including 1,000 heavy foot.

Source: Guide p.20. Rewritten in plain words.

RulerHis Most Warlike Majesty, King Ralff of the Fruztii
CapitalKrakenheim (pop. 3,300)
Population50,000+/-
Demi-humansFew
HumanoidsSome
Resourcesfoodstuffs, furs, silver, gold
Ruler's class and levelRalff, F 15 (Glossography p.17)

The Frost Barbarians are the weakest of the three Suel nations on the Thillonrian Peninsula, which these peoples call Rhizia. They never recovered from the Battle of the Shamblefield and have been under the overlordship of the Schnai for the past twenty years, as they were several times before. But the king the Schnai set on the Fruztii throne as a supposed figurehead has built up his kingdom carefully, and it is now independent in everything but its oath. A recent pact between the Fruztii and Ratik sent a joint army to wreak havoc in the Bone March; the next campaigning season it cleared the northern pass of the "Fists" (see Hold of Stonefist).

Source: Guide p.20-21. Rewritten in plain words.

RulerHis Pious Majesty, The King of Furyondy, Belvor IV
CapitalChendl (pop. 15,600)
Population350,000+
Demi-humansSome
HumanoidsDoubtful
Resourcesfoodstuffs, cloth, gold
Ruler's class and levelBelvor IV, P 14 (Glossography p.17)

The Viceroyalty of Ferrond was formed from several small states at the height of Aerdian power, around 100 CY, to give the Great Kingdom a strong western province from which to launch further conquests. The Viceroy ruled from the Clatspur Mountains to the Nyr Dyv, and from the Lortmils in the south to the far shores of Whyestil Lake and beyond in the north. As the power of the Malachite Throne in Rauxes faded (around 200 CY), the viceroys ruled more on their own authority and less by leave of their Aerdi overlords. The viceroyalty had become hereditary, and in 898 OR the heir of Viceroy Stinvri was crowned in Dyvers as Thrommel I, King of Furyondy, Prince of Veluna, Provost of the Northern Reaches, Warden General of the Vesve Forest, Marshal of the Shield Lands, Lord of Dyvers and so on. The outlying lands were soon lost, but the heart of the kingdom was sound and has lasted.

Belvor IV is a very noble and just king. His realm is closely allied with Veluna and constantly at war with the evil Horned Society and Iuz, and it sends troops on the Earl of the Shield Lands' expeditions against the Bandit Kingdoms. Furyondy's belled heavy cavalry is famous across the Flanaess, and so is its light infantry from the Vesve Forest. The standing army is only a few thousand strong, but in time of need the nobles' and militia contingents raise it to 20,000 or more. Furyondy's fleet completely controls Whyestil Lake, and a Furyondian squadron sails the Nyr Dyv from its base at Willip. The kingdom's colors are blue and red stripes.

Source: Guide p.21. Rewritten in plain words.

RulerHis High Radiance, Owen I, Grand Duke of Geoff
CapitalGorna (pop. 4,800)
Population65,000
Demi-humansHigh Elves (6,000), some others
HumanoidsSome (see Crystalmist Mountains)
Resourcescloth, copper, silver, gold, gems (I)
Ruler's class and levelOwen I, F 13/I 15 (Glossography p.17)

Geoff is ringed on every side by mountains, hills and forests, which has kept it almost free of the usual wars of the Flanaess, apart from a short conflict with Keoland around 450 CY. The Rushmoors mark its nominal eastern border. Its people are a Flan, Suel and Oerid mix that seems to combine the best of each, which is just as well, because fearsome ogres and giants keep coming down out of the Crystalmists. The Geoffites live in harmony with the elves of the realm, and the two often join forces against the invading monsters. Grand Duke Owen I is a clever, brave leader, on good terms with both the Earl of Sterich and the King of Keoland. His forces include cavalry, archers and companies of pikemen from the mountain holdings.

Source: Guide p.21. Rewritten in plain words.

RulerHis Most Resolute Magnitude, Petros, Commandant of Gran March
CapitalHookhill (pop. 4,500)
Population80,000
Demi-humansSome
HumanoidsFew
Resourcesfoodstuffs, cloth, copper, gems (III)
Ruler's class and levelPetros, F 15 (Glossography p.17)

Keoland created the Gran March early in its history, building it around a military and religious order of knights. These zealous warriors quickly subdued the feuding locals, imposed order and drafted every fit man into labor and infantry battles (units much like regiments). The land between the Lortmils and the Dim Forest, north of the Sheldomar, became productive and peaceful, but the first Commandants ruled harshly. When the ruler of the time, Berlikyn, fell fighting Veluna and Furyondy in the Small War, the people celebrated. Keoland then rethought its policy and let the people elect their own Commandant from among the noble houses of the Gran March. The state is now Keoland's vassal in name only and is on friendly terms with Bissel. The Commandant's army relies mainly on mailed cavalry: medium horse with lance, crossbow and sword.

Source: Guide p.23. Rewritten in plain words.

RulerHis Celestial Transcendency, the Overking of Aerdy, Grand Prince Ivid V of the North; Archduke of Ahlissa, Idee, and Sunndi; Suzerain of Medegia; Commander of the Bone March; Lord of the Sea Barons; Protector of Almor and Onnwal; Hetman of all the Aerdi; etc., etc.
CapitalRauxes (pop. 41,000 )
Population5,000,000 (includes N. and S. Province and Medegia)
Demi-humansSome (scattered on fringes of kingdom)
HumanoidsSome (mixture)
Resourcesfoodstuffs, cloth, copper, silver, gold, gems (IV)
Ruler's class and levelunnamed, C 7/MU 12 (Glossography p.17)

Everyone knows the Great Kingdom's history, so it is not repeated here. Once the greatest force for order and good, the Aerdians have sunk over the last century into appalling decadence. After a thousand years of leadership, their rulers and nobles turned to evil and madness. The present Overking, Ivid V of the royal House of Naelax, is said to be quite mad, yet cunning and capable in a devious way. His direct rule covers the Royal Demesne around the capital and the Grandwood; beyond that he governs only by threatening and persuading the peers whose fiefs make up the rest of the realm.

The Overking's Companion Guard is ten picked companies of mixed arms: heavy, medium and light cavalry, crossbowmen, archers, and five companies of foot with polearms. With the nobles' contingents he can put more than 15,000 troops in the field fairly quickly, and in an emergency four or five times that many.

The North and South Provinces are held by Aerdi royal houses as vassals and are run almost as independent states. Trouble in the Bone March has brought the Herzog of the North back into line, just as the struggle with the Iron League pushed his southern counterpart into closer cooperation with the Malachite Throne (see North Province, South Province and the See of Medegia). The Sea Barons pay the Overking a token tribute and carry on their piracy under letters of marque bearing his seal.

The Glossography lists the Overking's class and level without a name.

Source: Guide p.23-24. Rewritten in plain words.

RulerHis Solemn Authority, the Lord Mayor of Greyhawk, Nerof Gasgol
Population58,000 (city) 75,000+ (total, including surrounding area)
Demi-humansSome
HumanoidsSome
Resourcessilver, electrum, gold, platinum, gems (I-IV)
Ruler's class and levelNerof Gasgal, T 10 (Glossography p.17)

Greyhawk began as a trading post on the Selintan River during the early migrations. As it prospered, a local warlord built a small keep on the hills above the village of Greyhawk that had grown up around the trading center. He taxed the trade and now and then robbed caravans, especially those carrying silver ingots taken from the burial mounds of the Cairn Hills. This petty noble soon grew rich and powerful and took the title Landgraf of Selintan. Greyhawk and the Landgraf's power grew quickly from then on, and his son and heir Ganz married the daughter of the Gynarch (Despotrix) of Hardby, a sorceress of some fame.

Their descendants ruled a growing domain that reached its height around 375 CY under Zagig Yragerne, the so-called Mad Archmage. Zagig built the sprawling Castle Greyhawk, now a ruin, and poured money into the city to make it the "Gem of the Flanaess." His reign was strange in many other ways too, and no one was surprised when, after years of rule in which he never seemed to change or age, he was reported to have vanished. The castle was abandoned, supposedly because of a terrible curse, but the city itself went on thriving.

In 498 CY Greyhawk was proclaimed a free and independent city, ruling from Hardby on Woolly Bay to the Nyr Dyv, between the eastern folds of the Cairn Hills and the Gnarley Forest, including much of what is now the northern Wild Coast. Those lands were lost over the following decades, and falling trade seemed sure to make the city a backwater, until recent events. Several years ago a string of treasure hoards was found in or near Castle Greyhawk. Huge wealth poured into the city, and craftsmen and mercenaries flocked to the boom. Local lords used the flood of hard coin to revive the city, and it again rules a large area: all the land from the Nyr Dyv to the point where the Neen River joins the Selintan, including the mines in the Cairn Hills. The Despotrix of Hardby now pays Greyhawk tribute to avoid being swallowed by the growing city-state again.

The city is governed by its Lord Mayor, who is chosen by the Directing Oligarchy. The Oligarchy is made up of the Captain-General of the Watch, the Constable, the Guildmaster of Thieves, the Guildmaster of Assassins, and representatives of the Society of Magi, the Merchants' and Traders' Union, the Artisans' League and the clergy, from 12 to 18 Directors in all.

The Guide spells the Lord Mayor's name Nerof Gasgol; the Glossography spells it Gasgal.

Source: Guide p.24. Rewritten in plain words.

RulerThe Worthy Sir, Loftin Graystand, Mayor of Highfolk
Population2,500 (excluding demi-humans)
Demi-humansHigh Elves (5,000 ) and some others
HumanoidsNone
Resourcesgold
Ruler's class and levelLoftin Graystand, D 12 (Glossography p.17)

Highfolk matters, and stays independent, simply because it is the southern outpost of the elves of the Quagflow Valley, which they call the Fairdells. The town is a trading center with about 2,000 humans. It is well fortified and guards the elves' homeland, the 100-mile stretch of valley upstream between the southern arm of the Yatils and the Vesve Forest to the east. Many hamlets lie in lovely dales along the river. The Lord of the High Elves lives in the region with about 10,000 of his people, and many sylvan elves live along the edges of the Vesve on the east bank. The folk of Highfolk and its valley are at peace with their neighbors to north and south. The more restless sometimes join mercenary bands of Perrenland soldiers.

Source: Guide p.24. Rewritten in plain words.

Ruler(No organized government or single ruler)
Population20,000 (woodsmen)
Demi-humansHigh Elves (12,000), Sylvan Elves (9,000), Gnomes (4,000), Halflings (2,000 Tallfellows), Gray Elves (1,000)
HumanoidsSome (raiders only)
Resourcesgold, rare woods

As the entry for the town explains, Highfolk is mainly an elven realm. The humans living along the 100 miles of valley are either woodsmen who live in harmony with their demi-human neighbors, or hillmen allied with the gnomes. The Lord of the High Elves is treated as the nominal ruler, but only by general consent and respect; the word of the gnome prince, a village elder or the earl of a sylvan elf community carries just as much weight. All the peoples of the valley are independent and free-spirited, but in time of need they can raise a large force, including human longbowmen and many kinds of demi-human troops. The Knights of the Hart of Highfolk are chosen from the best elven and half-elven warriors of the valley. The people's main enemies come from the land of Iuz, slipping through the Vesve Forest.

Source: Guide p.24. Rewritten in plain words.

RulerThe Dread and Awful Presences, the Hierarchs (true names unknown)
CapitalMolag (pop 16,200)
Population45,000 (?)
Demi-humansVery doubtful
HumanoidsHobgoblins (12,000), others
ResourcesNone known
Ruler's class and leveltrue identities unknown (Glossography p.17)

This land was once a stronghold of the better organized humanoid tribes. Some decades ago a group of evil humans took it over; they are thought to have been discontented bandits, or at least to have had help from one or more bandit kinglets. Either way, the land between the Veng and Ritensa Rivers, north as far as the territory of the Rovers of the Barrens, is now firmly in the Horned Society's grip. The Society joins great numbers of humanoid troops with human organization and power. Its religion is devil worship, and its leading Hierarch is said to be an evil high priest of 18th level. The other leaders are reported to include a magic-user above 12th level, several other powerful clerics, a master thief of 13th level and three fighter Lords. Many bandit troops from the east are known to visit the walled town of Molag, and the Society is on good terms with Iuz.

Source: Guide p.24. Rewritten in plain words.

RulerHis Most Ferocious Majesty, Lolgoff Bearhear, the King of Cruski; Fasstal of all the Suelii
CapitalGlot (pop 5,100)
Population60,000
Demi-humansFew
HumanoidsLikely in mountains
Resourcesfurs, copper, gems (I)
Ruler's class and levelLolgoff Bearhair, F 14 (Glossography p.17)

The Ice Barbarians live along the bleak north and east coasts of the Thillonrian Peninsula. They raid their southern cousins, the Snow and Frost Barbarians, or join them in raids on Ratik or the richer Great Kingdom. In high summer they often go looking for a fight around the coasts of the Hold of Stonefist; the Cruski both hate and respect the grim people of that land. Their most hated enemies, though, are the Sea Barons. They attack Sea Baron ships on sight and often raid and loot their islands, usually at a cost. Lately these raiders have joined the Frost and Snow Barbarians to counter the growing strength of the Great Kingdom's and the Sea Barons' coastal defenses.

The Guide spells the king's name Lolgoff Bearhear; the Glossography spells it Bearhair.

Source: Guide p.24. Rewritten in plain words.

RulerHis Brilliant Lordship, Count Fedorik Eddri of Idee
CapitalNaerie (pop. 4,900)
Population60,000 +
Demi-humansSome
HumanoidsDoubtful
Resourcesfoodstuffs, copper, gold
Ruler's class and levelFedorik Eddri, F 14 (Glossography p.17)

When the South Province rose against the Overking and the Herzog, the nobles and men of Idee led the way. Idee is the land most exposed to Aerdian revenge, so the Count keeps a standing army to man and supply the chain of castles and forts along his northern border, and the militia is ready to take up arms at a moment's notice. Meanwhile Idee does a lively sea trade with Onnwal and Nyrond.

Source: Guide p.24. Rewritten in plain words.

RulerHis Resolute Honor, Cobb Darg, Lord High Mayor of Irongate
Population44,000 (city) 57,000 (total, including surrounding area)
Demi-humansMany
HumanoidsNone
Resourcesgems (II, III)
Ruler's class and levelCobb Darg, ? (Glossography p.17)

This large, thriving city lives on sea trade and on commerce between Onnwal and the east. Its mix of peoples and ideas gave it an independent spirit early on. As the Overking's rule grew more tyrannical, the citizens began to grumble, and the Lord Mayor led a delegation to the Herzog with their grievances. The envoys were jailed, given a sham trial and executed by ritual torture for the Overking's amusement (446 CY). The next year the whole south rose against the realm, and after a short struggle the Iron League was founded, an alliance of mutual support that helped the rebel states throw off the Aerdi tyrants. Irongate keeps a strong naval squadron and a large company of armored crossbowmen in the League's service. It can also raise 2,000 heavy militia infantry, well trained and in high spirits, armed with spetums or glaive-guisarmes and able to march within a day of being called.

Source: Guide p.25. Rewritten in plain words.

RulerIuz, Lord of Evil (evil Demi-god)
CapitalDorakaa (pop. 10,000 )
Population40,000
Demi-humansNone
HumanoidsMany (numbers unknown)
Resourcesfurs, electrum
Ruler's class and levelIuz, demi-god (Glossography p.17)

Iuz, old Iuz of the tales used to frighten children, may be human, or may once have been; no one knows for sure. He has ruled from the Howling Hills south to Whyestil Lake for far longer than any human lifetime. The lands between the Dulsi and Opicm Rivers are so steeped in evil that even the fearless Wolf Nomads and Rovers of the Barrens go through the Cold Marshes rather than set foot on the edge of Iuz's land.

For a time the land had no master, because Iuz himself was gone. For many decades, with no evil will to drive it, its wickedness lay fairly quiet, and its good neighbors prospered. The mad and merry Zagyg had trapped Iuz in a strange chamber deep under the ruins of Castle Greyhawk, one of nine powerful demi-gods held there. The prisoners were freed in 570 CY, and Iuz rules again, gathering his forces for some dark purpose. He has sworn to destroy Tenser the Archmage, Lord Robilar and the others who tried to kill him when his prison was opened.

Besides the many evil clerics, thieves, fighters, assassins and magic-users who have flocked to his grim banner, many of the foulest humanoid tribes have grown strong and stand ready to march. Thousands of goblins, orcs and hobgoblins are known to be under arms, adding to the human troops of his armies.

Source: Guide p.25-26. Rewritten in plain words.

RulerHis Peerless Majesty, the King of Keoland, Kimbertos Skotti; Lord of Gran March, Plar of Sterich; Protector of the South; etc.
CapitalNiole Dra (pop. 21,600)
Population300,000 (excluding dependencies)
Demi-humansSylvan Elves, Gnomes, Halflings
HumanoidsDoubtful
Resourcesfoodstuffs, cloth, gold, gems (III)
Ruler's class and levelKimbertos Skotti, R 14 (Glossography p.17)

Keoland was the first great kingdom of the Flanaess. Oeridian and Suel tribes mixed and joined to build a tolerant, prosperous realm that nominally took in many different demi-human groups as well. After several centuries of kindly rule, a line of ambitious kings took the Keoish Throne and set out to conquer. At the height of this empire-building, around 350-360 CY, Keoland ruled from the Pomarj to the Crystalmist Mountains, while its armies pushed into Ket and threatened Verbobonc and Veluna City. The Ketite campaign ended in disaster in two battles, at Molvar and Lopolla, and an alliance of Veluna and Furyondy ended the Keoish threat on that side (the book calls this war the Short War here and the Small War elsewhere).

At the same time, the elves within Keoland's borders objected to the King's warlike policies and began driving royal garrisons out of the Ulek provinces and Celene. In the struggle that followed, the freemen of the west sided with the demi-humans, and raiders in the far south took the chance to harry the Keoish coast from Gradsul to Gryrax.

King Tavish III died fighting the Sea Princes at the Siege of Westkeep (453 CY). His son Tavish IV changed course the moment he took the throne. After long negotiations the Yeomanry was recognized as an independent state, the Ulek states were given self-rule, and Keoland went back to its old tolerance and prosperity. The semi-independent Gran March and Earldom of Sterich are loyal to the crown and send strong contingents to the royal army.

Keoland is known for its light cavalry, who use javelins, crossbows and lances. Most of the army is foot armed with polearms and long spears, and the nobles form the heavy cavalry. Small companies of elves, gnomes, halflings or dwarves usually turn out as well. The fleet is fit for battle but small, and the conflict with the Sea Princes still troubles the realm.

Source: Guide p.26. Rewritten in plain words.

RulerHis Illustrious Glory, Zoltan; The Beygraf of Ket and Shield of the True Faith
CapitalLopolla (pop. 23,400)
Population85,000
Demi-humansFew
HumanoidsFew
Resourcessilver, gems (I, IV)
Ruler's class and levelZoltan, C 3/F 14 (Glossography p.17)

Ket is the Baklunish frontier state and a trading hub between the eastern Flanaess and the lands beyond. For many decades it has menaced the Oeridian and Suel states to its east and south, at times invading them. Despite constant war, the land prospered from rich trade with the Paynim tribes, Tusmit, Ekbir, Perrenland, Bissel and Veluna, and goods from Zeif and Wintershiven pass through Lopolla. The mixing of cultures extends to the people: Ketites are of mixed blood, though mostly Baklunish in culture. The Beygraf's court is an odd blend of eastern and western ways, and so is the army, which fields strong units of pikes and crossbows alongside its light horse archers and medium lancers. The army is kept sharp, because in spite of shared blood and trade, the Paynim clans often raid the border lands west of the Tuflik River.

Source: Guide p.26. Rewritten in plain words.

RulerHis Exalted Highness, Prince Latmac Ranold of Duxchan; Lord of the Isles; Scourge of the Waves
CapitalSulward (pop. 5,500)
Population80,000
Demi-humansFew
HumanoidsDoubtful
Resourcesrare woods, spices
Ruler's class and levelLatmac Ranold, F 16 (Glossography p.17)

This scattered principality covers seven large islands from Spindrift Sound to the mouth of the Tilva Strait. The islands are rich and fertile and make the most of their strategic position. They profit enormously from cargoes carried from Hepmonaland to the Great Kingdom and take tribute from states that want to trade through the Tilva Strait. The rulers of Duxchan gave up piracy for more profitable ways of getting money from merchants. For obvious reasons the Sea Barons and the Lord of the Isles are bitter enemies. The Duxchaners are still smarting from the Battle of Medegia (572 CY), when the Sea Barons sank four of their warships and captured three loaded cogs before they could reach safety in Pontylver.

Source: Guide p.26. Rewritten in plain words.

RulerHis Equitable Nemesis, Spidasa, the Holy Censor of Medegia
CapitalRel Astra (pop.39,800 )
Population250,000
Demi-humansSylvan Elves (see Grandwood Forest)
HumanoidsSome
Resourcesfoodstuffs, cloth
Ruler's class and levelSpidasa, C 15 (Glossography p.17)

The Holy Censor was first the chief cleric of the Great Kingdom. The clergy were granted lands from Rel Astra to Pontylver, south of the Mikar and Flanmi Rivers, including part of the Imperial Preserve (the Grandwood Forest). When the Malachite Throne declined, the fief became strong enough to be independent in all but name. The Holy Censor is still one of the Overking's chief advisers, though, and rules his peasant masses harshly with Rauxes' full blessing. The See's clerics and nobles have grown very rich. Their mercenaries harass the elves of the Grandwood and plunder across the Flanmi in the Glorioles and the Hestmark Highlands, where the Censor has pushed his holdings right up to the foothills and fights the dwarves and gnomes there without mercy.

Source: Guide p.26-27. Rewritten in plain words.

RulerHis Radiant Grace Grenell, the Herzog of the North Province
CapitalEastfair (pop. 29,100)
Population750,000
Demi-humansFew
HumanoidsSome
Resourcesfoodstuffs, cloth, electrum
Ruler's class and levelGrenell, A 15 (Glossography p.17)

The Herzog of the North Province is the Overking's cousin, as evil as his kin but certainly not as mad. His princely fief runs from the Blemu Hills to the shores of the Solnor Ocean and south to the Adri Forest, well below the Trask River. The court at Eastfair is notorious for its debauchery. The North Province has been shaken by the advance of Nyrond and Almor into the lower Bone March and their capture of Knurl, along with continued humanoid raids from across the Teesar Torrent. A mercenary force sent to punish the raiders was recently beaten in the hills above Bellport (printed "Belport" here), and the Herzog is now said to be asking the Overking to pay for a huge army to retake the southern Bone March. Such a force would surely include both hired men-at-arms and humanoids recruited from the upper march.

Source: Guide p.27. Rewritten in plain words.

RulerHis August Supremacy, King Archbold III of Nyrond; Duke of Flinthill; Altmeister of All the Aerdi, etc.
CapitalRel Mord (pop. 46,500)
Population1,375,000
Demi-humansSylvan Elves, Gnomes, Halflings
HumanoidsFew
Resourcesfoodstuffs, cloth, copper, silver, gems (I, II)
Ruler's class and levelArchbold III, F 16 (Glossography p.17)

Nyrond's strength, and the hostility of its kings and nobles toward the Great Kingdom, have been the main shield of the civilized nations against the raids of the Great Kingdom and its mad emperors. Nyrond itself went through a period close to empire-building, when it made the County of Urnst and the Theocracy of the Pale pay tribute for a while. That changed when the wise King Dustan I, called the Crafty, saw his realm threatened by unrest at home and enemies abroad and called the Great Council of Rel Mord. There the king met envoys from Almor, the Iron League, the Pale and Urnst. Afterward all troops were pulled out of the Pale and Urnst, which were allowed to govern themselves, and both agreed in return to a pact of mutual trade and military support. Almor was treated in much the same way, and the Iron League was given loans and treaties that ensured its survival against their common enemy.

Nyrond's borders now run along the Nesser River, the Franz River, the Artonsamay River, the Nutherwood, the northern end of the Gamboge Forest, the Rakers, the Flint Hills, the lower Harp River and Relmor Bay. Nyrond sends troops to help Urnst and the Pale against the Bandit Kingdoms, and a squadron of its warships sails Relmor Bay and the Sea of Gearnat in support of the Iron League. Strong garrisons are posted where they can march quickly to help Almor or the Pale.

Besides its human forces, Nyrond has special demi-human scouts, and in time of need treaties bring help from the County and Duchy of Urnst and others. Heavy cavalry and armored foot make up most of the army, supported by smaller numbers of archers and light hillman infantry.

Source: Guide p.27. Rewritten in plain words.

Onnwal began as a minor fief of the Herzog of the South Province, his to grant to loyal followers. The Great Kingdom's oppression bred deep discontent and then open revolt, until the whole South Province was in arms. When the Iron League was founded in 447 CY, the empire lost all of the southern part. The League bound Onnwal in an economic and military alliance with the Free City of Irongate (which closes off the Onnwal peninsula), Idee, Sunndi, and the demi-humans of the Glorioles and the Hestmark Highlands. Onnwal and Irongate provided the sea power and the others the land forces, though Onnwal and Irongate sent strong contingents to the land battles as well.

Aerdian forces besieged Irongate for several months. At the Battle of a Thousand Banners a trick panicked the northerners and broke the siege, and a combined army of League men and gray elves then cut down great numbers of them. Onnwal has never been invaded, but the Herzog's squadrons raid it by sea from time to time, which is why its main port, Scant, is so heavily fortified. Apart from a small regular force and its marines, Onnwal relies on levies in time of war.

The Flan tribes of the Yatil Mountains were far more warlike and fierce than most Flan elsewhere. These strong clans absorbed the newcomers who came to conquer them: Oerids, Suel and even a few Baklunish. Mountaineers and valley folk alike fought hard against attempts by Furyondy, and later Ket, to expand into Perrenland. Those attempts, and raids by nomads, drew the clans together around 400 CY into a loose union under the banner of the strongest of them, Perren. The clan holdings were divided into cantons, and the clan leaders (hetmen, voormanns or whatever they called themselves) elected a chief executive, something like a king with limited powers, to rule for eight years with the advice of the assembled leaders. The system has worked well, and Perrenland is fairly prosperous from trade with the northern nomads, the Baklunish states, and Veluna and Furyondy.

Its chief export, though, is its well-trained mercenary bands. A typical band is 30% pikemen, 20% mountaineers with polearms, 30% lowland crossbowmen and 10% other foot with battleaxes, flails and the like; the last 10% is cavalry. Half the horse is heavy, mostly from around Schwartzenbruin, and half is medium cavalry with bows from the Clatspur region. Perrenland does not claim the Quagflow Valley below the Clatspurs, but high elves from there often serve with Perrenland bands as scouts and light infantry with bows, usually adding about 10% to the human force. Such mercenaries are found in the armies of Veluna, Furyondy and Bissel, and even Ket hired them in a quarrel with Tusmit.

Perrenland always keeps a close watch on every border. Its permanent garrisons are quite small, but excellent militia can be raised in a single day to back them up. A small squadron of warships is enough to keep Lake Quag Perrenland's private water, and the same ships escort merchant barges and cogs going downriver.

Source: Guide p.28. Rewritten in plain words.

Only a small part of the rolling plains roamed by the nomadic Baklunish tribes lies within the Flanaess. That part is sometimes almost empty of people and at other times said to swarm with horsemen. The nomads apparently leave the Dry Steppes when summer turns them into a parched waste and return in the rainy season. The tribe of Ull holds a permanent territory, of course, and the northern plains belong to the more civilized states along the Dramidj Ocean.

Each tribe is ruled by a noble called an Amir or Khan. Greater nobles are called Ilkhan, Orakhon or Shah, and leaders of royal rank Tarkhan, Padishah or Kha-Khan. The northern and western tribes use Amir, Shah and Padishah, while those from the south (the Dry Steppes) prefer Khan, Ilkhan and so on. The Tiger and Wolf Nomads also use Khan and its related titles, so it is thought that they are branches of the same people, split apart by later nomads who brought in the Amir titles.

These horse nomads wear little armor but are very mobile. The most lightly equipped carry short, powerful horn bows and light curved swords; the rest (20% to 30%) carry light lances and maces or flails. Little else is known. The western states such as Ket, Tusmit and Ekbir often hire bands of Paynim nomads to fight one another or other raiding nomads.

This rich peninsula was once a group of petty states under the protection of the Prince of Ulek. Unhappy with that, their nobles broke their oaths, threw the Prince's garrisons out of his castles and took the castles for themselves. For several decades the Pomarj prospered in its new freedom, as the mines of the Drachensgrab and the sea trade made noble and commoner alike rich.

Then came the Hateful Wars (498-510 CY). The united Ulek states, helped by Veluna and the demi-humans of the Kron Hills, broke the hordes of Euroz and Jebli that had nested in the Lortmils and were trying to spread into the lands around them. The humanoids were finally driven out and scattered. Some fled north toward the Yatils, but most, under wiser leaders, went into the Suss Forest and from there to the rugged mountains of the Pomarj. Finding the humans there weak and lazy, they struck fast, seized the strongholds and made themselves masters of the whole peninsula. There are surely renegade humans helping them, and hired mercenaries as well, paid with gold from the Stoneheim mines and with moonstones and cairngorms from the high peaks.

A relief force of dwarves and men sent by the Prince crossed the Jewel River but was driven back after a fierce battle below the Hilly Pastures. The humanoids have rarely dared to cross into Ulek, but their raiders cause much trouble along the Wild Coast.

When the Overking created the Bone March he wanted another outpost beyond it, and the Aerdi banners pushed north as far as the Timberway. A military commander was appointed to secure the territory, and logging began, since the great pines there were prized for shipbuilding. The commander was a just man, friendly with the dwarves, and a capable tactician. He sent such a stream of riches south, along with detailed reports of victories over the last Frost Barbarians in the area, that the Overking took notice. After the commander soundly beat a raiding fleet, the Overking made him a noble, Baron Ratik. His descendants have ruled the fief ever since, fighting raiders so bravely that they won their respect and even the friendship of some, while humans and demi-humans alike prospered.

When the humanoid hordes began their attacks, the mountain dwarves gave Ratik plenty of warning. Companies of men and gnomes hurried west to help their countrymen against the invaders, and messengers rode south (and north) to raise the alarm. Resistance was so fierce that the attackers went around Ratik and fell on the Bone March instead. The isolated barony has since been ruled as a palatine fief.

The Baron's forces can defend Ratik but are not strong enough to drive the humanoids from the mountains and plain to the south. The baronial levies are schiltrons of spearmen and a small body of light cavalry. Large dwarven contingents and several companies of sturdy gnomes are available when needed. The regular army is men-at-arms, crossbowmen and mounted sergeants, with woodsmen armed with bows patrolling the north and hillrunners with slings watching the southern borders.

The city and constabular fief of Rel Astra runs from the city north to the Lone Heath south of the Mikar, and includes the town of Ountsy, whose mayor answers to Rel Astra. This trading port is held as a hereditary fief by an Aerdi noble house that is secretly plotting against the royal House of Naelax, though it takes care that no proof ever reaches its enemies. It badly wants close ties with Medegia and the Sea Barons to balance the power of the Overking's kinsmen in the North and South Provinces. The Overking is said to watch these schemes with barely hidden delight, seeing them as a useful check, since he fears his own family at least as much as he distrusts everyone else. At the same time, the lord of Rel Astra wants to stop the Censor's lands from growing, and he is rumored to be plotting secretly with the free folk of the Grandwood Forest and the Herzog of the South Province.

The Constable Mayor keeps a strong force of cavalry and foot and a squadron of warships. His cavalry is built around about 100 nobles and knights, whose esquires and sergeants add some 400 medium horse; light horse bring the total to a full 1,000. There are as many men-at-arms, about half of them crossbowmen. Levies and militia of 1,000 horse and 6,000 foot can be raised from Rel Astra, Ountsy and the surrounding lands at short notice. Lately Rel Astra has used mixed bands of humans and orcs as light scouting troops in the Grandwood, and similar bands on the Lone Heath.

The nomad tribes living between the Wastes below the Icy Sea and the Fellreev Forest called themselves the People of the Plentiful Huntinglands. Their neighbors named them the Rovers of the Barrens, because they had no permanent settlements and their land looked bleak. These hardy nomads were content with their herds, their hunting and an occasional raid on Furyondy, the Bandit Kingdoms or Tenh. The growing power of the bandits and the swelling numbers of humanoids, though, have badly cut down their lands, numbers and strength.

At the great Battle of the Opicm River, the full might of the Rovers gathered to fight a combined army from the land of Iuz and the newly formed Horned Society. The Rovers' wardog soldiers and light cavalry were cut to pieces and scattered, and many of their chiefs were killed. Perhaps three or four clans of only a few tribes each are all that is left of the force that once sent the Wolf Nomads' tumans fleeing back across the Dulsi without their gray-tailed banners. A people who once roamed freely from the Dulsi and Veng Rivers to White Fanged Bay and the Zumker River is now a handful of warriors huddled between the Wastes and the Forlorn Forest.

Their light cavalry use lance and javelin, and many also use bows; picked men use lariats to drag enemies down. Some tribes provide excellent medium horsemen as shock troops. The wardogs are foot soldiers who can run alongside the cavalry and fight, hamstringing enemy mounts and breaking up their formations.

It is said that long ago an order of monastic warrior-priests was founded on the remote plateau south of the closed city of Kro Terlep. The order is said to hold that the Suel are the rightful rulers of all the Flanaess and superior to every other race, and to embrace evil as the only way to reach that goal. The Scarlet Brotherhood is supposedly the fruit of those plans, and it now controls all the land from the Vast Swamp to the tip of the peninsula.

Brothers of the Scarlet Sign are said to be hidden as trusted advisers or servants in many courts and castles of the north, spying for their master and waiting to strike. According to the tales, the Brotherhood has three rings: thieves at the bottom, assassins above them, and the smallest and highest ring, the monks, on top. The head of the thieves is called "Elder Cousin" and the head of the assassins "Foster Uncle," so other thieves are called "cousins" and assassins "nephews." The Brotherhood's temple and monastery is said to be a fortress and walled town in its own right, guarded by soldiers, by humanoid legions being readied for future conquest, and by monsters trained to serve it.

The buccaneers of the Azure Sea and Jeklea Bay grew strong and rich while Keoland was at its height, because Keoland's leaders had their eyes on empire in the north and ignored the sea raiders. These privateers began calling themselves Sea Princes, after one especially successful captain who really was of noble birth. Sailing unopposed from their island and mainland strongholds, they plagued the coasts from Gradsul to Scant and the Pomarj, and beyond into the Sea of Gearnat and the Tilva Strait.

When Keoland gave up its imperial ambitions, it rebuilt its navy to deal with the Sea Princes, as they were now generally called. By then they were so numerous and strong that the Keoish fleet, even with a squadron of Ulek warships, could only deal them a sharp setback (the Battle of Jetsom Island). That lesson made their leaders rethink their ways. Several of the wiser captains retired to estates on the mainland and put lieutenants in charge of their ships, sending them not to raid the Flanaess but to sail to the Amedio coast and bring back rare woods, spices, ivory and gold taken from the jungle peoples, to trade in the north. In time the Sea Princes' mainland lands grew larger than their islands, and they did little formal raiding.

Today they are probably still the strongest sea power, but they also have a small, efficient army and are fairly peaceful traders. Their one great fault is that they allow slavery, despite strong protests from the Yeomanry. The Prince of Monmurg is said to want to end it, but his fellow nobles block him: the Prince of Toli, the Plar of Hool and the Grandee of Westkeep, along with the Commodores of Jetsom, Fairwind and Flotsom.

The Snow Barbarians are the strongest and most numerous of the northern peoples. Several decades ago they took the west coast below Glot and have held it ever since. For a time the King of the Schnai had the Frost Barbarians under his thumb, but the Fruztii are now free in all but their pledge. That has not spoiled relations with either neighbor, since all three see the Great Kingdom and the Sea Barons as their natural source of easy loot. Fighting invading humanoids has become a national pastime, but there are always enough men left to crew the longships when the season for raiding the south comes round.

The Baron of Ratik is rumored to have proposed to the King of the Schnai a four-way alliance to take the Hold of Stonefist and the Bone March. Under the supposed plan, the Schnai might gain Glot and Krakenheim, the Fruztii and Cruski would split the Hold, part of the Timberway would go back to the Frost Barbarians, and Ratik would rule the Bone March. How the Schnai will respond is anyone's guess, but they are surely watching the recent joint ventures of the Fruztii and Ratik closely.

The ruler of the South Province, a cousin of the Overking in Rauxes, is out of favor. Every attempt to win back the lost parts of his fief has failed, and the money flowing to the Malachite Throne has dropped sharply, since the lost lands were very rich. So the Herzog has declared that he will stake his whole personal fortune on one last attempt to break the Iron League. Success would make most of his titles more than empty words, restore him to favor in Rauxes, fill his treasury to bursting and give him a great deal of wicked satisfaction besides.

For now his holdings are only the fief of Ahlissa and the central lands the Herzogs have always kept, around Hexpools and the Thelly River, and the Censor of Medegia, eager to profit from the Herzog's disgrace, claims part even of that. The native troops are unreliable at best, apart from those of the petty nobles and gentry who serve the Herzog, but his heavy cavalry is thought to be very effective, and his hired men-at-arms are exceptionally well armed and equipped, which makes the Army of the South a dangerous force. If the Herzog keeps his vow, a major war can be expected soon, and if it comes, Nyrond and Almor will surely move to support the Iron League of Idee, Irongate, Onnwal and Sunndi.

The Spindrifts are the easternmost islands of the Asperdi-Duxchan chain, about 100 leagues east of the Medegian coast. Exact information is lacking, because neither the Sea Barons nor the captains of Duxchan have reported on them; both probably hope to add the islands to their own holdings. Tales say many elves live in the Spindrifts, and that neither seafaring nation reports anything because the elves capture and imprison any sailor bold enough to enter their waters. The southernmost isle was once ruled, the stories say, by a mighty wizard named Lendore.

The Spindrifts are known to fall into two parts: the northern islands of the high elves, and the single southern island, Lendore Isle. The three northern islands are said to be overseen by five elven wizards, supported by many elven lords and half-elven clergy. Ships from the Lordship of the Isles and from the Sea Barons that have gone there have yet to come back. No towns or villages have been reported in the northern islands; these demi-humans seem to want only to be left alone.

Lendore Isle, by contrast, trades a great deal with the mainland, and through the Council of Seven of Lo Reltarma it pays generous sums to both the Lordship of the Isles and the Sea Barons for safe passage. Now and then some bold pirate ignores this protection and is later wiped out, whether by an agent of the Council or someone else is not known. The humans of Lendore Isle worship almost nothing but the ancient Suel gods, and how that faith came to rule such a distant island is a mystery. The island is named for the Archmage who founded its civilization, but the tales of him and the company he brought to the Spindrifts are all but lost.

Stonefist, then called Vlek Col Vlekzed, founded his chiefdom around 430 CY. The Rovers of the Barrens had thrown him out for banditry and lying, but a few warriors and their families followed him. For several years he wandered the edges of his homeland, raiding and robbing everyone alike. These small successes drew a growing band of outcasts, bandits, criminals and other unsavory types. With this odd mix of fighters he led a very successful raid into Tenh, swung down into the Bandit Kingdoms to gather more followers, and then beat a punitive army sent from Tenh. When a bandit kinglet threatened him, Vlek took the man's stronghold by surprise, sacked it and carried off most of its people.

Riding unchallenged through the lands of his old people, though not caring to test their fighting skill, Vlek moved on beyond White Fanged Bay and built a fortified settlement as a permanent camp. He tricked the people of the area, the Coltens Feodality, into talks, then slaughtered their envoys and escort, routed the rest of the Coltens army by surprise and ferocity, and settled down to rule the whole territory. As his infamy spread, malcontents from many nations flocked to his banner, despite his new name of Stonefist, which meant both a terrible enemy and an unbending ruler.

The Mastership of the Hold is partly hereditary. Vlek's descendants (he had 219 wives and 351 sons who lived to adulthood) compete in a "Rite of Battle Fitness" (printed as bi-annual). The winner may challenge the Master or one of the Atamans of the three towns, or lead a warband as its chief. The surviving losers join the standing warbands, the "Fists," and those who did best become chieftains, sub-chiefs and raid leaders. These savage war bands often raid the Fruztii, Tenh and even the Rovers of the Barrens.

About 30% of the Hold's people live in permanent settlements, and most of the foot soldiers come from them. Most of the rest are semi-nomads who move into the northern tundra in summer and come back south in autumn. The Fists' horsemen and light infantry come from them.

The County of Sunndi was once a fief within a fief, granted to a loyal peer of the Herzog of the South Province. After years of crushing taxes, abuse by the royal troops and the Herzog's alike, and harassment of its demi-humans, the human and demi-human nobles of the region joined the general rising against Aerdian rule, and in 455 CY Sunndi joined the Iron League.

Natural barriers make the county easy to defend: the dense Rieuwood, and hills to the east and west. South of Sunndi, the neck of the Tilvanot Peninsula is plugged by a huge half-salt swamp, a mixed blessing since many very unpleasant creatures live there. The county profits from its natural resources, farming included, and from trade, by land with Idee and by sea with Duxchan. But it is constantly threatened by the Herzog's legions from the north, the Holy Censor of Medegia's forces from the east, and the Sea Barons along its coasts.

Sunndi's troops are always under arms: human and dwarven companies in the Glorioles, human and gnome companies guarding the eastern hills, and human and elven foresters ranging the northern woods. The hillmen use slings and morningstars; the men of the interior prefer crossbows and bardiches. Apart from the nobles and their equerries, Sunndi's cavalry is medium or light, and there is not much of it, since Sunndi relies on its ally Idee to the west to provide horse.

The western shores of the Sea of Gearnat have long been called the Wild Coast, because the region has always been a refuge for malcontents, dissidents, demi-humans, humanoids and the outcasts of other states. It is pleasant land but not especially fertile: rolling country broken by woods, fens and scattered clusters of houses. Parts of the Gnarley Forest, all of the Welkwood east of the Jewel River, and the Suss Forest are counted as part of the region. The Wild Coast remains free territory, a mix of petty nobles, robber barons, guild-run towns, fishing and forest villages, freebooters, mercenaries and displaced people of every sort. That is because it is remote and isolated, has few resources and has never been strategically valuable. At various times Celene, the Prince of Ulek, the Gynarch of Hardby and the Free City of Greyhawk have controlled parts of it, but its people, who see things differently, have always won their freedom back.

Across the Flanaess the Wild Coast is known as a place of refuge, a very dangerous one and at the least full of adventure. Its mixed peoples are well known as mercenaries and adventurers, and the region produces many outstanding clerics, fighters, magic-users and thieves. Its legendary sons include Mordenkainen, Robilar and Tenser, among others.

Tales tell of a lost city of the Old Suel somewhere in the Suss, from which the Jewel River got its name. It has never been found, and the legend is very doubtful. With the Pomarj in the hands of greedy humanoids, the southern Wild Coast has been an unhealthy place in any case, and for obvious reasons no one has lately tried an expedition into the Suss Forest.

The people who settled the land west of the Javan River, north of the Hool Marshes and below the Jotens, were mixed Flan and Suel tribes. Some Oeridians came too, and the first settlers accepted them as long as they did not trespass on the lands or rights of those already there. These peoples took to holding a yearly meeting of all the tribes, where disputes were settled and agreements of every kind made. All warriors were equal, but each tribe named one spokesman for every dozen. As numbers grew this became one for every twelve dozen, and the twelve spokesmen elected a thirteenth to speak for all.

This democratic custom survived when the region came under Keoish rule. Despite its remoteness the Yeomanry did a lot of trade with the kingdom, because it was very rich. The Keoish exploited the people, but they also brought them many benefits. The Keoish king treated the yeomen as gentlefolk and their spokesmen as lesser nobles, giving the region a voice in council and a window on the wider world. Many thousands of yeomen served in the Keoish army for decades. When the kingdom began its wars of conquest, though, the freemen rose and shut their border to Keoish rule for good. They succeeded mainly because the kingdom faced rebellion on every side, and the result was a state governed by all its warriors through election. Everyone who bears arms or has borne them, and all artisans and craftsmen, may now vote for spokesmen.

The Freeholder must be elected from among the several score greater landowners, but he answers to the council of Common Grosspokesmen. He runs the government and directs the Free Captains of the Battles.

The Yeomanry's soldiers are mostly spearmen and crossbowmen. The mountaineers provide heavy troops with polearms and light slingers, and the greater freeholders supply the small cavalry contingents. Demi-humans, who are also voters, are called up in time of need, so when the army marches it brings elven spear and bow units, dwarven mailed foot and halfling light troops.

Good, Evil, Law and Chaos

A country's political system matters, but so does how much its people and rulers respect life and order, as shown in its laws. These attitudes are very subjective, but they can be measured roughly. The Guide includes a map showing, very roughly, how good and evil, law and chaos, are spread across the Flanaess. Light areas are closely tied to good. Areas shaded gray are given over to evil or lean toward it, and travelers cross them at risk to their lives. Medium areas call for some caution but are safer and more tolerant than dark ones. Symbols mark how much each region respects law and property; regions given over to chaos are especially dangerous for travelers and merchants and are seldom crossed.

Regional Products

A second map shows the main goods each country exports. Not all of this trade happens through formal agreements, and not every item is exported all year round. The Resources line of each state's summary lists the same goods.

Source: Guide p.46-48. Rewritten in plain words.

Where no figures are given for a place in this chapter, the chronicler knew too little about it to estimate them.

Azure Sea

One of the main trade routes between the western and central nations. Freebooters are fairly common, the savages of the islands off the Amedio coast take up piracy, a few other pirates work the east, and the Sea Princes are not above some buccaneering now and then.

Nyr Dyv (Lake of Unknown Depths)

The largest freshwater lake known, though tales speak of a true inland sea far to the west, if they can be believed. A great deal of trade crosses the lake, which has many navigable rivers flowing in (the Artonsamay, Veng and Velverdyva) and out (the broad Nesser, and to a lesser degree the Selintan). Its central position and these river routes make it the busiest water in or around the Flanaess. Admundfort, Radigast, Leukish, Dyvers and even Greyhawk depend heavily on its shipping. Squadrons of warships patrol it constantly to keep raiders down and fight off the occasional predatory water creature.

The Rhennee

One of the lake's oddest features is the people who live on great barges, trading, fishing and earning their whole living from the Nyr Dyv. Lake Quag sometimes freezes over much of its surface and Whyestil Lake is cold and unhealthy in winter, but the southern shores of the Nyr Dyv stay fairly pleasant all year, and the bargefolk winter there. They are shrewd traders and able fighters, so few bother them. Some say they are skilled thieves and pirates; nothing has been proven, though it is quite possible, and the bargefolk hotly deny it. They call themselves the Rhennee. They travel every river and lake connected to the Nyr Dyv that their barges can navigate, but always come back to the Nyr Dyv for the winter.

A typical barge is 12 to 18 feet wide and 30 to 45 feet long, with a lug sail; larger ones usually add a gaff sail rigged aft. They can also be moved with sweeps and poles. Their draft is shallow, but the hull is deep enough to be decked over, with a small cabin just behind the middle. The rails are planked over for protection and carry many heavy crossbow mounts, and some barges have scorpions at bow and stern. Each barge has a "lord," who lives in the cabin with his family, and "cousins," servants who may or may not be kin and who live on or below deck, for 15 to 20 people in all. Every adult and able youngster works and is trained to fight. When "camped," the bargefolk chain their vessels together, which also serves as a defense. Most barges carry a small boat for messages, fishing or ferrying.

The bargefolk are said to have an elaborate signaling system using flags by day, colored lanterns by night and sometimes smoke, and a special cant that only other Rhennee understand. If they really are as rich in gold, jewelry and prized freshwater pearls as the stories say, nothing about their homes, clothes or habits shows it.

Lake Monsters

The Nyr Dyv is also known for its monsters. Huge creatures lurk deep below, preying on careless sailors or anyone unlucky enough to fall in. Warships, and sometimes merchants or bargefolk, bring such monsters back as trophies; constant war against them is needed to keep the lake usable.

Lesser Bodies of Water

Aerdi Sea. The waters from the Tilva Strait to the northern tip of Asperdi Island, out as far as the islands beyond Spindrift Sound, roughly bounded by the islands along the east coast of the Flanaess. There is much sailing here, and many monsters on and under the waves. See also Spindrift Sound.

Densac Gulf. Thought to run a thousand miles south between Lower Oerik and Hepmonaland. Who sails it and what lies beneath is unknown.

Dramidj Ocean. This ocean stretches far to the west. Warm currents from that direction sweep past Zeif and Ekbir and turn north. In winter it is wrapped in thick fog banks, and huge blocks of ice drift across it like ghost ships.

Gearnat, Sea of. Crowded with shipping coming down the Nesser, crossing, or heading to or from the Azure Sea. It is treacherous in spring and autumn, when great storms whip it into towering waves, and in summer raiders from the Wild Coast, the Pomarj and elsewhere make sailing risky.

Grendep Bay. This great arm of the Solnor Ocean is the northern barbarians' favorite route for raiding the mainland. These bold sailors try to cross south as early in spring as they can and return late in autumn, because in the warm summer great sea monsters are often seen playing in the bay.

Icy Sea. The Solnor sweeps north around the Thillonrian Peninsula and ends here. These waters are frozen except in high summer. The northern barbarians sometimes take their galleys in to hunt for ivory and furs, with a little raiding on the side. Even in summer thick fogs and floating mountains of ice make it dangerous.

Jeklea Bay. This small arm of the Azure Sea is little more than the Sea Princes' private lake. Only their ships sail it, raiding into Amedio and coming back loaded with plunder.

Oljatt Sea. The waters north of Hepmonaland and east of the Duxchans. These warm, deep, blue-green waters are extremely dangerous because so many creatures haunt them, some big enough to drag a ship to the bottom. Ships entering the Oljatt are said to chain themselves together and keep men with pikes and bows ready to fend off monsters.

Quag, Lake. The third largest freshwater lake in the Flanaess. Perrenland is the only civilized nation on its shores, so the lake is entirely theirs. It yields a lot of food, though sometimes the fishers get eaten.

Relmor Bay. The part of the Gearnat between Nyrond and the South Province. Ships from the southern Great Kingdom rarely make the long voyage around Onnwal through the Azure Sea and the Densac, round the Tilva Strait and north up the coast, or the reverse. So ships met here are either trading between Almor, Nyrond and Onnwal, or hunting those that do, most likely the Ahlissan squadron based at Prymp Town.

Solnor Ocean. Said to stretch a thousand leagues and more to the east. The Sea Barons are rumored to have sailed some distance east and come back, but this has never been confirmed. Great monsters live in the Solnor and play in Grendep Bay when the sun warms the water.

Spindrift Sound. Scene of some of the fiercest sea fights, because when the Sea Barons meet ships of the Lord of the Isles, no quarter is asked or given. Unknown pirates and buccaneers also haunt these waters, which keeps things lively.

Tilva Strait. This narrow channel between the cockscomb of Tilva and Hepmonaland is the only way between the central and eastern waters. Pirate ships, sometimes whole fleets, prey on the traffic, so warship squadrons patrol when important trade is at its peak.

White Fanged Bay. Named for the great ice-coated rocks and icebergs, shaped like a predator's teeth, that threaten ships trying to land on its shores. In summer seals, walruses and stranger creatures bask on its rocky coasts, and hunters come for ivory and furs. Some say the name really comes from the long tusks taken from these animals rather than from the icicles and frozen spray.

Whyestil Lake. Bordered by Iuz, the Horned Society, Furyondy and the Vesve Forest. Before the evil of Iuz rose, much trade crossed it to and from Dorakaa and Crockport and up and down the Veng from the Nyr Dyv. Only the Veng traffic remains, and even that is very dangerous. Furyondy keeps a strong fleet on the lake, but Iuz's vessels are many, and the Horned Society threatens the river traffic.

Woolly Bay. No one remembers the joker who gave this end of the Sea of Gearnat its name and made it stick, but it fits: the small cogs that sail up and down the Wild Coast are as often pirates as merchants. Much traffic passes through from the west and from Greyhawk, rounding the Pomarj or Onnwal to and from the Sea of Gearnat. Elredd, Fax, Safeton and Hardby are all ports, most ships can sail up the Selintan to Greyhawk City, and lighter craft can go on to the Nyr Dyv. Some unscrupulous captains still put in to trade at Highport, a town held by humanoids.

Source: Guide p.48-51. Rewritten in plain words.

Abbor-Alz

The rocky hills running east and west between the Nesser River and Woolly Bay. Their northern edges are fairly safe and are claimed by the Duchy of Urnst, as are the gentler highlands covered by the Celadon Forest. The middle and south are very dry, and wild tribesmen living there turn back every intruder, if the intruder gets back at all. The hills are so rough and steep that horses cannot cross them, nor can organized bodies of soldiers, so no attempt to clear these heights has ever worked. Now and then adventurers come back with tales of prospecting there and meeting natives and monsters, but most such stories cannot be believed. There certainly is wealth in the Abbor-Alz, though, since Urnst runs productive mines in the part held by the Duchy.

How far the hills run into the Bright Desert is unknown. The peoples living in and beyond the Abbor-Alz are as unfriendly as the hill tribes.

Cairn Hills

The arm of the Abbor-Alz that thrusts north. These hills surround Midbay on the Nyr Dyv and form the borderland between the lands claimed by Greyhawk City and by the Duchy of Urnst. Several thousand gnomes live in the middle of the hills, halflings enjoy the lower northern slopes, and many dwarves live where the hills meet the Abbor-Alz and rise into young mountains. In the very rugged back country below Midbay, strange burial sites have been found from time to time. These rich tombs belong to a people unknown even to the demi-humans, who apparently lived before them. Those who found them came back with terrible tales of horrid guardians, death and worse, but also with ingots of precious metal, gems and other treasures. The tombs gave the hills their name and draw many foolhardy adventurers.

There are no settlements east of the marshes along the Upper and Lower Neen Rivers until the eastern edge of the hills.

Hestmark Highlands

These hills run north along the coast of the South Province from the town of Dullstrand to the mouth of the Flanmi, with a branch running northwest into the Glorioles. They have always been a rallying point for discontented humans, because their remoteness and rugged ground have let their demi-human inhabitants stay free of the Overking and his servants. Many gnomes and dwarves live here, and free-spirited men have villages in the shelter of the hills too. The area is known for precious metals and gems, so the Overking's forces, badly in need of wealth, often raid it: Medegians, the Herzog of the South Province's troops and imperial soldiers all probe the hills far too often. The people, tough from the start, have become hardened veterans through these endless skirmishes, and together with the men and elves of Sunndi they are starting to raid the lowlands beyond in revenge. The independent town of Dullstrand (pop. 5,500) and the land around it declare themselves neutral, but they probably help the rebels in secret. Freebooters certainly find safe harbor there, and its forges turn out weapons and armor the Overking and his men never see.

Kron Hills

Nearly 20,000 gnomes are thought to live in the Kron Hills. The hills run east from the Lortmils almost to the Nyr Dyv. Their edge forms the southern border of Veluna, then runs beside the Velverdyva for a while before rising in the heart of the Gnarley Forest, where many sylvan elves happily roam the hilltops. Their southern slopes mark the end of the Wild Coast region and belong to northern Celene. There are some dwarven settlements where the Krons meet the Lortmils, though their numbers are unknown. The gnomes of these hills helped organize the army that drove the humanoid hordes out of the Lortmils (and the Krons), and they fought with honor in the army that beat the Horde of Elemental Evil in the battle above Verbobonc.

The Krons are mined for metals, precious metals and gems. The upper slopes are very fertile, and many crops grow in sheltered valleys and glens. Many scattered human communities live in peace with the gnomes and other demi-humans, except in the Gnarley Forest, where the elves keep to themselves.

Lesser Hills and Highlands

Blemu Hills. This chain runs from about level with Bellport south to the town of Knurl, with the Teesar Torrent cutting along its eastern edge. It forms the southeastern border of the Bone March. Demi-humans once lived here, but now tribes of Celbit, Jebli and Euroz infest it.

Bluff Hills. The western end of the Griff Mountains slowly breaks down into rugged ridges and steep hills, which separate the Bandit Kingdoms from the lands of the Rovers of the Barrens. The bandits now hold and claim the Bluff Hills, as they do all of the Fellreev Forest, and the nomads to the north are too weak to stop them. The hills are said to hold small deposits of copper and gold. Many monsters roam here, and many ogre bands make it their home.

Drachensgrab Hills. These hills surround the low mountains of the same name in the Pomarj. Rich in valuable minerals and gems, they have always been home to many terrible beasts and monsters that the humans of the coastal lowlands had to contend with. Now that the humanoid hordes hold the area, many of these monsters will surely be recruited into their ranks. Legend says one or more powerful creatures lie at rest in these hills and may one day return to life.

Flinty Hills. This broad, deep band of hills marks the southern end of the Rakers. Its eastern shoulder, and an arm reaching many leagues south, form the southern border of the Bone March and the easternmost lands of Nyrond and Almor. The part covered by the Adri Forest, west of the Harp River, belongs to Almor. The area is rich in minerals. Many halflings live in the south and many gnomes in the north. The far western stretch of the Flinty Hills lies within the Gamboge Forest.

Good Hills. Rolling highlands in Keoland, running from east of Sterich to the middle of the border with the Yeomanry, with the Javan River as their western edge. Many halflings and gnomes live here, and the hills hold considerable mineral wealth.

Gull Cliffs. The headlands that rise steeply along the coast west of the Sea Barons' islands, named for the many seabirds nesting on the hills and sea cliffs (also written Gullcliffs). The town of Roland lies among these hills, a major port for trade between Rauxes and the sea.

Headlands. The heights of the middle of the Onnwal Peninsula. This spine runs from the city of Irongate along about half the peninsula, forming cliffs on the Azure Sea coast. Many dwarves and some gnome groups live here.

Hollow Highlands. The north-south chain of hills dividing Idee from Sunndi, named for the mining and burrowing done there over so many years. Dwarves, gnomes and halflings live here. The hills are no longer very rich in minerals or gems, but their beauty and fertility keep the demi-human population high. The Overking's servants do not enter the Hollow Hills without strong forces.

Howling Hills. These hills lie just below the southern edge of the Cold Marshes, with one part split from the rest by the valley of the Dulsi River. The eastern hills now belong to Iuz and are surely home to all sorts of hideous creatures and savage humanoid tribes who mine their metals. The western part is sacred to the Wolf Nomads as a burial ground, and they have fiercely defended it against any intrusion by men or humanoids from Iuz. Several large battles are said to have been fought in and around the wedge of hills between the Blackwater and the Dulsi for this reason, and Iuz does not like being thwarted.

Iron Hills. The highlands running east from the city of Irongate and marking the boundary between Ahlissa and Idee in the west. Most of these hills are held by the Iron League. The mines yield very high grade iron ore and several kinds of precious metal, much of it dug by dwarves and gnomes.

Little Hills. The Jotens become very high hills as they reach the Javan River valley, and these hills turn south as if following the river. They are "little" only next to the Jotens and Crystalmists beyond, which is clearly how the yeomen who named them saw it. Many demi-humans live in the Little Hills, along with communities of men. The town of Longspear, in their foothills, is a busy trading center. Soldiers from this area, human and demi-human alike, are famous for their ferocity in battle.

Lorridges. Sharp ridges and hills at the northern end of the Lortmil Mountains, where some dwarves and gnomes have homes and mines. They are split about evenly among the Gran March, Bissel and Veluna. The pass between these hills and the foothills of the southern horn of the Yatil Mountains is the main entrance to the eastern Flanaess. The Yatil foothills are called the Northern Lorridges, but they belong to Highfolk, and their gnomes serve the elves.

Sepia Uplands. Perrenland now claims most of this block of highlands, the lower heights of the Clatspur range. The Wolf Nomads hunt in the northern part, and the hills inside the Vesve Forest are claimed by no humans. Some mineral deposits are suspected here.

Spine Ridge. The unhealthy Vast Swamp is bounded on the south by a chain of rising hills that end in a great plateau in the middle of the Tilvanot Peninsula. These hills are said to be rich in precious metals and gems but are too dangerous to mine normally, being home to many humanoids and monsters.

Stark Mounds. The many spurs of the Crystalmists push some low mountains and high hills east toward the Javan River below where the Realstream joins it. They divide Geoff from Sterich and are probably old, worn mountains. They end at the east bank of the Javan and are claimed mostly by Geoff. Some dwarves live in the steeper parts, but they are mainly home to gnomes.

Tors. The mesa-like hills at the end of the last spur of the Crystalmists. Bordering the Hool Marshes, they mark the southern edge of the Yeomanry. These wild hills are a constant headache for the yeomen, since they are home to many kinds of monsters and humanoid tribes.

Tusman Hills. Highlands that form the border between Ket and Tusmit and eventually rise into the Yatils. Their hillmen are famous fighters, which keeps them semi-independent; they gladly serve as mercenaries for both Tusmit and Ket.

Yecha Hills. These Yatil foothills are rich in minerals, and the Tiger Nomads have actually started mining them. Their capital, Yecha, is a permanent settlement in these highlands, and many of their herdsmen graze sheep and goats here.

Source: Guide p.51-52. Rewritten in plain words.

Cold Marshes

The vast fens and bogs north of the Howling Hills separate Blackmoor from the lands of the Wolf Nomads and the Rovers of the Barrens. The Dulsi and Opicm Rivers rise here, both feeding the great Whyestil Lake. There are said to be riches in the highlands south of the marsh, but only the very brave or the very foolish go near it, because the Cold Marshes are best known for the vile creatures in their mires.

Vast Swamp

Above the neck of the Tilvanot Peninsula the land narrows to only 30 leagues across. It is sunken in the middle and cliffed along both coasts, so water gathers in standing pools and sluggish streams, and the resulting mass of water and plants is the Vast Swamp. The upper swamp begins below the middle of the Hollow and Hestmark Highlands, which flank it to west and east. It runs south for well over 200 miles, more than 150 miles across at the top and narrowing to only 30 miles at the bottom, where the Spine Ridge rises. The water slowly drains south, but no river is known to flow out of the far end, so it is thought to run off through underground channels.

Some desperate outlaws live in the Vast Swamp, along with native humans and humanoid tribes, bullywugs especially. Fierce predators and loathsome monsters also claim it. The men of Sunndi and the hill folk on either side keep constant watch to make sure the swamp's dwellers do not wander beyond its edges. There are many tales about the place, the most likely being that of the lost tomb of the demi-lich Acererak, who once ruled the swamp and the cockscomb of Tilvanot beyond.

Lesser Marshes and Swamps

Gnatmarsh. A large area of very treacherous wetland along the east bank of the Nesser from the Celadon Forest to below where the Duntide joins it. Many ghastly creatures live in these bogs, and they breed countless millions of biting insects in summer.

Hool Marshes. After the Hool River rushes down from the high lake and streams of the Hellfurnaces, it wanders across the plains, and most of its length is surrounded by quaking mires and bottomless pools. This makes a natural border between the Yeomanry and the Sea Princes' lands to the south. Renegade humans, humanoids and many kinds of monsters live here.

Lone Heath. This great marsh, east of the mighty Grandwood Forest, is where the Mikar River rises. It gives refuge to human and demi-human outlaws fighting the evil and oppression of the Overking and his servants. Unlike most such places, evil things are afraid to enter the trackless Lone Heath.

Pelisso Swamps. Unhealthy stretches along the north coast of Hepmonaland. They are unexplored, and who or what lives there is unknown.

Rushmoors. A long stretch of marsh east of the middle Javan to the headwaters of the Sheldomar. It forms part of Keoland's northern border and belongs to the unclaimed region made up of the central Dim Forest, the eastern Oytwood and the Rushmoors. Many dangerous creatures live in the marshes, and humanoid bands are reported there too.

Troll Fens. The chill mists of the Troll Fens, against the shoulders of the Griff Mountains and the Rakers at the head of the Yol River, hide unspeakable horrors. The Pale hems the place in with watchtowers and keeps, and strong patrols ride the southern edges constantly, watching for unwelcome visits from the monsters and humanoid bands within. As the name says, the fens are infested with many particularly huge and vicious trolls.

Source: Guide p.52-53. Rewritten in plain words.

Corusk Mountains

The Corusks form a bow along the backbone of the Thillonrian Peninsula, running from the Solnor Ocean in the east north and west, then southwest to their end at Hraak Pass. Humans live on the lower slopes, but bands of evil humanoids and monsters of every sort live in the high interior. The range is thought to hold little valuable ore or gems.

Crystalmist Mountains

The highest range in the Flanaess. It begins where the Ulsprue and the Barrier Peaks meet and runs southeast to the Hellfurnaces. West of it lie the Dry Steppes, while several small states nestle against its eastern slopes, where spurs reach north and east. Many kinds of monsters, humanoid tribes, and many giants, ogres and the like live among its high peaks and strange valleys. Even so, men often go into the range looking for precious metals and gems, since unusually bold and hardy mountain dwarves live there too. A great glacier in the middle of the range is the source of the Davish River, which flows through Sterich to join the Javan.

Griff Mountains

As the name suggests, many monstrous creatures live on these peaks. The Griffs run from the western end of the Corusks at Hraak Pass southwest and west for more than 100 leagues, dividing the Hold of Stonefist from the Duchy of Tenh and the Theocracy of the Pale to the south.
